bg: esdras, the second book of

This exists in a Latin translation, the Greek being lost. Chapters 3-14 consist of a series of angelic revelations and visions in which Ezra is instructed in some of the great mysteries of the moral world, and assured of the final triumph of the righteous.
Asia

Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2. Proconsular Asia contained the seven churches of the Apocalypse (Rev. 1:11).
ch.s: Verses 1–10: “Woe to you, Babylon, and Asia! Woe to you, Egypt and Syria!”; Verses 11–20: “The Lord will threaten, and who will not be utterly broken in pieces at his presence?”; Verses 21–30: “Behold, food will be so cheap on earth that they will think themselves to be in good condition, and even then calamities will grow on earth: sword, famine…”; Verses 31–40: “even so in those days, there will be three or four left by those who search their houses with the sword.”; Verses 41–50: “He who sells, let him be as he who flees away, and he who buys, as one who will lose.”; Verses 51–60: “Therefore don’t be like her or her works.”; Verses 61–70: “He formed man, and put a heart in the midst of the body, and gave him breath, life, and understanding”; Verses 71–78: “They will be like mad men, sparing none, but spoiling and destroying those who still fear the Lord.”. Places: Babylon, Asia, Egypt.
q: Read verses 1–10. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
